subject: URGENT: Starlite experiencing 5xx/429 spike — Dedicated pool capacity exhaustion / autoscale lag
messages:
From: Dana Park <dana.park@starlite.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@starlite.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Spike of 5xx/429 from your hosted/dedicated pool — urgent

Hi Soojin / Laura,

We started seeing a sudden spike of 5xx and 429 errors around 08:40 PDT from our API calls to your endpoint (starlite-dedicated-01). Error rate is ~18% over the last 10 minutes and we're also seeing many client-side timeouts. Retries are piling up on our side and latency has jumped from ~220ms to >2s for many requests.

This is affecting our production users. Can you confirm whether there's a capacity issue on the Dedicated pool or an autoscale lag? We don't see any changes on our side. We're happy to provide logs (attached a quick screenshot) and collaborate.

Thanks — please escalate.

— Dana

Subject: INTERNAL: Starlite outage — suggested immediate runbook steps

Internal — copying the customer's report below for context. Key ask: confirm capacity state for starlite-dedicated-01 and execute emergency mitigations. Proposed immediate actions: 

- Opened PD-1234 (link in metadata).
- Scale up Dedicated pool by adding prewarmed instances (+2–4 GPUs) to relieve queueing.
- Reduce autoscale cooldown from 120s -> 45s temporarily and increase min_instances by +2 to avoid evaporation during bursts.
- Enable routing fallback to hosted-fallback-uswest (lower throughput model) for new requests from Starlite while we recover.
- Temporarily raise per-customer concurrency cap to limit retry amplification.
- Collect detailed perf traces (qps, queue length, GPU utilization, pod startup times) and tar logs into pd-1234-logs.tar.gz.

Attachment: runbook-dedicated-autoscale.pdf (short checklist)

Please confirm when each action is started/completed and post links to Grafana panels for the pool. If we need exec visibility (credits / SLA exception), let me know and I'll loop Marcus/Laura.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:25:03 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Starlite outage — immediate actions taken

Status update — actions executed and initial findings: 

- Scaled starlite-dedicated-01 by +4 GPUs (added 2 prewarmed nodes and 2 standard nodes).
- Adjusted autoscale policy: min_instances +2, cooldown 120s -> 45s, provisioning hysteresis loosened for bursts.
- Rolled temporary routing for new requests to hosted-fallback-uswest which uses a smaller model variant (gpt-lite-1). That cut median latency immediately for new requests.
- Discovered a rapid burst of prefix-heavy requests that were filling the KV cache and extending per-request GPU time; queue depth hit >500 and token processing latency spiked, causing upstream 5xx timeouts and client retries.
- Disabled aggressive client retry header at edge (edge proxy now returns 429 with Retry-After when concurrency exceeded), added a short per-customer concurrency cap for Starlite to prevent retry amplification.
- Collected logs and exported traces to pd-1234-logs.tar.gz. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/starlite-dedicated-01 (mirrored to oncall channel).

Early result: error rate dropped from ~18% -> ~0.7% over the last 10 minutes; latency back to ~260–320ms for most requests. Monitoring closely.

Next: we should schedule an RCA to analyze autoscale timings and warmup latency, and evaluate prewarming strategy for high-QPS customers.

— Dev
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

We will still need a full RCA and a proposal for preventing recurrence (prewarm guarantees? SLA / credits conversation). Please include expected timeline for RCA and an initial summary for our execs.
